# A `return` inside an `if` or a `for` returns from the function. The
# interpreter read a body by scanning its top level for a Return and executing
# everything before it, so a return written one block deeper was executed as a
# statement that did nothing and the guard clause fell through to the line
# after its `if`. Every backend emitted the right code, so only the test runner
# and the constant folder disagreed with the program -- which is what makes
# this a txtar test: the testdata harnesses check, they do not run.
sngl test guards.sngl
stdout '4 tests, 0 failures'

# Same program, same answers, through a real backend.
sngl generate --platform html --lang none -o out guards.sngl
grep 'return "zero"' out/index.html

# A zero-arg computed is called where its result is what the position wants.
# The for iterator was the one place that did not, so `for c = letters` failed
# to check at all.
sngl test iterate.sngl
stdout '1 tests, 0 failures'

-- guards.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import . "sngl:test"

func sign(n int) string {
    if n < 0 {
        return "negative"
    }
    if n == 0 {
        return "zero"
    }
    return "positive"
}

// The base case returns from inside the `if`; the recursive call stays in tail
// position, so this is also the shape the interpreter trampolines.
func repeat(s string, n int) string {
    if n <= 0 {
        return ""
    }
    return s + repeat(s, n - 1)
}

func firstNegative(xs list<int>) int {
    for x = xs {
        if x < 0 {
            return x
        }
    }
    return 0
}

component main {
    var n = 0
    func label() => sign(n)
    text #out(value=label)
}

func testConstantFolded(t Test, c main) {
    t.assert(sign(-2) == "negative")
    t.assert(sign(0) == "zero")
    t.assert(sign(7) == "positive")
}

func testAtRuntime(t Test, c main) {
    t.assert(c.out.value == "zero")
    c.n = 5
    t.assert(c.out.value == "positive")
}

func testRecursionTerminates(t Test, c main) {
    t.assert(repeat("ab", 0) == "")
    t.assert(repeat("ab", 3) == "ababab")
}

func testReturnOutOfLoop(t Test, c main) {
    t.assert(firstNegative([3, 1, -4, -1]) == -4)
    t.assert(firstNegative([3, 1]) == 0)
}

-- iterate.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import . "sngl:test"

component main {
    var word = "abc"

    func letters() => string.split(word, "")

    vbox {
        for c = letters {
            text(value=c)
        }
    }
}

func testComputedIterator(t Test, c main) {
    t.assert(c.letters().length() == 3)
}
